 ORANGEBURG, S.C . – The North Carolina Central University football program will head to Oliver C. Dawson Stadium on Saturday for a first-place showdown against the Bulldogs of No. 18/20 South Carolina State.
 Kickoff is set for 1:30 p.m. The game will air live on ESPN+, then re-air on ESPNU Sunday at 9 a.m. and Monday at 9 p.m. 
 The Series: This will be the 31st meeting between the Bulldogs and the Eagles. The Eagles trail in the all-time series 13-17. The Bulldogs have won five of the last six meetings; NCCU last won in 2023, 62-28 in Durham. Head coach Trei Oliver is 1-5 against South Carolina State.
 Eagles on the Road: NCCU is 20-19 on the road under Oliver following last Saturday's comeback win over Norfolk State. The Eagles have been .500 or better on the road in each of the last three seasons. The Eagles were 5-1 on the road last season. They went 2-2 on the road in 2024, and 3-3 in 2023. In 2022, when NCCU won the MEAC title, the Eagles were 4-2 on the road.
 Last Time Out: NCCU caused a turnover in the final minute, then Joshua Jones found Mekhi Wall for the game-winning touchdown as the Eagles defeated Norfolk State 29-28. The Eagles have won three straight games. Running back Gino Addison recorded his third 100-yard rushing game in the last four, going for 174 yards on 18 carries. Addison averaged 9.7 yards per carry. Quarterback Jousha Jones had four touchdowns on the afternoon: three passing, one rushing. Jones tied his career high for touchdowns in a game, matching the four he scored against Delaware State on Nov. 23, 2024. Defensive back John Clifford, Jr., recovered a fumble late in the fourth quarter to set up the game-winning drive. His first recovery of the season gives the Eagles an FCS-high 21 turnovers forced on the year. The Eagles have recovered nine fumbles in 2026. Linebacker Jayden Walker led the Eagles defense with nine tackles.
 NCCU vs. the MEAC: Since Oliver took over as head coach, the Eagles are 25-11 in MEAC play – including a 3-0 mark so far this season. That includes a stretch from 2021-24 in which NCCU went 4-1 in league play each season. The Eagles were 3-2 in the MEAC in 2025. NCCU won the MEAC title in 2022, before defeating Jackson State in the Celebration Bowl.
 Scouting the Bulldogs: South Carolina State, ranked 18th in the AFCA Coaches poll and 20th in the STATS Perform FCS poll, is 8-2 overall and 3-0 in MEAC play after defeating Howard 35-28 this past Saturday. Like NCCU, the Bulldogs have won three straight games. The defending champion Bulldogs were picked to repeat as MEAC champions this season. SCSU leads the MEAC in both scoring offense and scoring defense, putting up more than 41 points per game, while holding opponents to under 18 points a contest. The Bulldogs also lead the conference in total offense and total defense. SCSU leads FCS in total defense and sits second in scoring offense, while also ranking top 10 in total offense and scoring defense. Running back Mason Pickett-Hicks is second in the MEAC in rushing, just shy of 80 yards per game, while quarterback Keely Watson is second in the conference in passing. Ka'Von Chisolm leads the MEAC in sacks and ranks third in tackles for loss. He is tied for eighth in FCS in sacks and 13th in tackles for loss.
 The Coaches: Trei Oliver (NCCU, 1998) is in his seventh season as a college head coach. With 24 years of college coaching experience that includes five conference championships and three Black college football national titles, Oliver returned to his alma mater as North Carolina Central University's 24th head football coach in December 2018. 
 South Carolina State head football coach Chennis Berry enters his third season at the helm of the Bulldogs program after quickly establishing one of the top runs in the Football Championship Subdivision and HBCU football. In just two seasons, Berry guided South Carolina State to back-to-back MEAC championships in 2024 and 2025, including the program's 20th MEAC title overall. 
 Defense Getting Greedy: Through 10 games, NCCU's defense is tied for the FCS lead with 21 turnovers, including nine recovered fumbles and 12 interceptions. That includes four turnovers at East Carolina – a game in which the Eagles recovered three fumbles and one interception. The Eagles have forced four turnovers in a game twice this season: vs. North Carolina A&T and at East Carolina. Junior defensive lineman Zarion Walters is tied for eighth in FCS with two fumble recoveries. The Eagles have 12 interceptions on the season after recording two against the Bison, and they are tied for third in FCS in that category. A recovered fumble in the closing minutes on Saturday keyed the Eagles' comeback against Norfolk State.
 Addison Racking up the Miles: Freshman running back Gino Addison has 100-yard rushing games in three of his last four games, including his career-high 214-yard performance at Delaware State. Against the Hornets, Addison ran 31 times for those 214 yards, finding the end zone twice. This past Saturday against Norfolk State, Addison rushed for 174 yards on 18 carries. He also celebrated Homecoming with 169 rushing yards against William & Mary. For the season, Addison leads the MEAC with 88.8 yards per game on the ground. He has 710 yards on 101 carries for the season, with three touchdowns.
 For more information on NCCU Athletics, visit NCCUEaglePride.com.
